readout_other: self-reported visual percepts (drawings and survey questions) while viewing a crosshair
direction_notes: Participants given a random mix of sham and actual diagnostic ultrasound reported illusory visual percepts more often (53.7%) than a sham-only group (36.3%), with reporting likelihood increasing over the experiment.

exposures.label: Diagnostic ultrasound (Sonosite L25x) over visual cortex, 15 s exposures

target.label: visual cortex, at the location where TMS elicited phosphenes

device.model: L25x 13-6 MHz transducer on a Sonosite M-Turbo Ultrasound system

timing.protocol_description: Device in penetration mode at highest gain, mechanical index 0.7; each trial was 2 s ramped pink noise, 15 s of sham or actual ultrasound with constant pink noise, then 2 s descending noise, followed by 45 s drawing and 30 s survey. 20 trials after a sham baseline trial: 14 actual and 6 sham in random order for the mixed group; a separate group of 10 received sham only.

source_quotes.n_subjects: For the 11 participants exposed to a combination of sham and actual ultrasound, six of the subsequent 20 trials were assigned as sham ultrasound trials, whose distribution was determined using a random number generator, with unique distributions for each participant.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: In the present study, the transducer had a range of 6–13 MHz, and setting the device to penetration mode pushed this close to 6 MHz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: After exposure to sham or actual ultrasound for 15 s interleaved with pink noise as described above, there followed a drawing phase (45 s), during which the participant drew what they observed.

flags.reason: 21 participants took part: 11 received a random mix of sham and actual ultrasound, 10 sham only. Recorded the 11 who received actual ultrasound.
